messages:
Maya: Dropping a working doc idea. We need a compact launch checklist for the long-term routing/isolation project that ties to customer commitments and OKRs. Keep it deployable in phases.
Omar: Agreed. My strong preference is feature-flagged rollouts + progressive traffic ramp. Avoid any global config flips.
Priya: Draft gates I care about: measurable isolation (noisy tenant impact <5% p99 on neighbors), policy correctness (policy precedence deterministic), and variant telemetry (per-model-variant p90/p99).
Sam: Ops wants concrete thresholds: alert at p95 increase >20% or p99 increase >10% for more than 5m. Also need circuit-breaker for a tenant: drop to 5qps when error budget exceeded.
Jordan: Customers keep asking for two things: 1) per-tenant burst pools they can draw from, 2) hard data-residency controls so traffic never leaves a region unless explicitly allowed. Both need to show in contract checklist.
Tess: Legal: residency must be self-certifiable in the UI and auditable in logs for SOC/ISO. Need an acceptance test to prove no cross-region egress in sample workload.
Maya: OK proposed phased launch personas: "Preview" (internal + opt-in customers), "Committed" (reserved lane + SLA), "Enterprise" (VPC + hard residency). Each persona has gating criteria.
Maya: Example launch gates (short):
1) Observability: per-tenant and per-variant dashboards + 30d cost attribution
2) Canary: <0.5% traffic with auto-rollback on regression
3) Isolation: synthetic noisy-tenant test passes (neighbors p99 delta <5%)
4) Economics: routing policy does not increase median cost/response >12% for baseline workloads
5) Compliance: region_residency=true honored in routing + audit logs preserved
6) Recovery: automated eviction and warm-fallback completes within 120s
Omar: For implementation this implies three deliverables: a) policy DSL + precedence rules, b) routing controller with affinity + fallback, c) rollout system integrated with canary service.
Priya: On the DSL side I propose we treat model_variant as a first-class match key. Sample snippet to show intent:
```
routing:
  - when: tenant.residency == "eu"
    match: model_variant in ["quant4_kv","int8_small"]
    action: route: eu-isolated-pool
  - when: tenant.tier == "committed"
    action: reserved_lane: committed-pool
  - fallback: regional-affinity -> best-effort-global
```
Sam: Load test plan (brief):
- Run mixed synthetic traffic at 2x nominal for 90m
- Inject a noisy tenant generating hot key churn; measure p50/p95/p99 for neighbors
- Trigger forced eviction path and validate failover + queue drain within 2 minutes
- Simulate region outage and assert residency-constrained tenants do not cross-region
Jordan: Sales needs a customer-facing checklist: latency SLOs per persona, residency guarantees, burst pool sizing guidance, and legal-safe wording for residency. I'll draft the checklist.
Tess: I'll coordinate acceptance language. Also ask: are we recording per-tenant egress paths in an immutable audit trail? That's required for some contracts.
Maya: Yes, audit trail must include routing decision, model_variant chosen, and HSM key id if KMS used. Add that to gate 1 (Observability).
Omar: One open question: how strict are we about model-quality regressions when routing to quantized variants? Priya: Gate = automated eval on customer prompt set with <1% L1 metric regression, otherwise policy must be opt-in.
Sam: Ops ownership: I propose SRE owns runbook + rollback hooks, Eng owns controller, Arch owns DSL & gating matrix, Product owns persona mapping & customer commitments.
Maya: Action items and owners:
- Priya: full gating matrix with test definitions (due Tue EOD)
- Omar: RFC for controller + rollout integration (Wed)
- Sam: load test plan + runbook (Wed)
- Jordan: customer checklist & contract language (Thu)
- Tess: audit/log acceptance criteria (Thu)
deploy-bot: FYI: staging deploy window Fri 01:00-05:00 UTC. Please tag PRs with "routing-gates".
Maya: Let's reconvene Friday 10am to review drafts. Keep notes tight, this will feed the Q3 roadmap doc. Thanks :raised_hands:
